clue.text: Barren setting for model and German artist

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model can give T
und is German for and
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A bleak location chosen for a photo shoot with a German painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and German' reads as a link plus an adjective, but together they give UND, the German word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless Arctic plain, a bleak and empty landscape or setting.

clue.text: Game finds defender loading empty gun with bullets

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football or hockey

indicators.note: loading a gun puts something inside it, so the ammunition goes within the other piece
an emptied word loses its inside letters, keeping only its first and last

parts.note: bullets are ammo, ammunition

explanation.surface: A defender loads an emptied gun with bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the gun to its outer letters and 'loading' signals the insertion; 'defender' is a sporting position, not a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Alternative title for books on decoration

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a title is a name
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a different title for books about decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a decorative object, so the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Slimy, backward dregs of humanity embracing Open University

indicators.note: embracing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
backward tells us the word for the dregs is written right to left

parts.note: scum is a contemptuous term for the lowest people
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, a British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A scornful dismissal of the slimy lowlifes who signed up for distance learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the dregs word around, and 'embracing' then holds the university initials inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucous describes something covered in or like mucus, which is slimy.

clue.text: Motorway pile-up with hospital involved: a confused mess

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so one letter goes within the crash word

parts.note: a pile-up is a smash on the road
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A motorway crash with a hospital caught up in it leaves a chaotic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 was Britain's first motorway, written with a letter I in crosswords; 'involved' puts the hospital letter inside the crash word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a jumbled muddle of things, so it is a synonym for a confused mess.

clue.text: Unknown hack to go to court over dish

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed over another sits above it, so the earlier words come before the last letter

parts.note: to hack is to chop
to sue is to take legal action in court
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous journalist takes legal action over some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down answer means CHOP SUE stands above Y; 'hack' looks like a journalist but means CHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop suey is a Chinese-American dish of stir-fried meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Hard rain falling on the dragon

indicators.note: falling suggests the letters tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A downpour lands on a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' rearranges HARD RAIN. 'dragon' here is a fierce old woman, not the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, scolding old woman, and dragon is slang for exactly such a person.

clue.text: Rising temper is a foregone conclusion

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: temper and mood both mean a state of mind

explanation.surface: Someone's rising anger was always bound to end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' in a down clue turns MOOD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a fate that cannot be avoided, an outcome decided in advance.

clue.text: Ungenerous approach

definitions.meaning: old-fashioned for stingy, mean with money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stingy as an adjective and to draw closer as a verb.

clue.text: Substandard rum to toss around

indicators.note: around tells us the throwing word goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to shy is to throw or fling
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Poor-quality liquor fit only to be thrown about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is British slang for strange; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means badly made, of poor quality, so it is a synonym for substandard.

clue.text: Corral by which holy man keeps house in state

parts.note: the OK Corral, scene of a famous gunfight, is the corral named by these letters

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the holy man goes round the house

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk or priest

explanation.surface: A cattle pen where a priest keeps his house within a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The OK Corral in Tombstone was the site of a famous Wild West gunfight; 'keeps' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Failure is about to enter partnership

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these pieces go into the partnership word

parts.note: marriage is a lifelong partnership
taken as written
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A marriage on the rocks as something comes between the partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' is the container signal; 'Failure' is meant in the sense of a miscarriage of justice, not pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscarriage, as in a miscarriage of justice, is a failure to reach the right result.

clue.text: Reward fellow member in strangely serene surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings go around something, so the shuffled letters wrap round the other pieces
strangely says these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: CO is short for company, a fellow or companion
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Honouring a colleague in a calm setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges serene, split into two parts that wrap round the fellow and member pieces, as 'surroundings' says; 'fellow' is a companion here, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A recompense is compensation or payment given for something, a reward.

clue.text: Release catch and have wild fun with a gun

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of control into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Instructions to free a lock and then go crazy with a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns FUN into UNF; the Sten gun was a British wartime submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to undo a fastening, freeing the catch that holds something shut.

clue.text: Father, perhaps, to tear about continually

indicators.note: about says the tearing word goes round the outside of the other

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
ever can mean always, continually

explanation.surface: A priest dashing about without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' means rip here, not dash; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a clergyman, and Father is one such title, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: The worst place one can be — in pocket of thin coat

indicators.note: in places the worst place inside the pouch

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or pocket in a plant or animal

parts.words: The worst place one can be
parts.note: hell is the proverbial worst place to be

explanation.surface: Finding yourself trapped in the pocket of a flimsy jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thin coat' suggests a garment but means a layer of varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish brushed on in a thin protective layer.

clue.text: Left fat pig inside

indicators.note: inside puts the pig within the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A fat pig has been left indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is the definition, a nautical term, not a verb; 'inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical word for port, the left side of a ship.

clue.text: Inmate arranged early start for show

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a different order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A prisoner sets up an early opening for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges INMATE into MATINE; 'start' takes E from early.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance, a type of show.

clue.text: Protest, showing some degenerate tarts no mercy in return

indicators.note: in return means coming back, so the letters read backwards
some says only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Objecting by treating some depraved women mercilessly in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ETARTSNOMER from the run of words, and 'in return' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to object forcefully, a synonym of protest as a verb.

clue.text: Hammer-wielder taking short chopper to chest

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god who carries a hammer

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: an axe is a chopper

explanation.surface: A hammer-wielder takes a small axe to someone's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the E from AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the part of the body between neck and abdomen, the chest.

clue.text: A place to hide the port

parts.note: a den is a hidden lair or hideaway

explanation.surface: Somewhere to hide the bottle of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen.

clue.text: Speaking philosopher's jargon

indicators.note: speaking tells us the word is said aloud, matching a different spelling

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker's specialist terminology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking' turns KANT into a word said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is the special language or jargon of a particular group.

clue.text: Medic has a try to catch little monster

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
to have a go is to have a try
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A doctor attempts to capture a small beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' looks like a container signal, but here it is NET, the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a small or young dragon; it is also a small fish.

clue.text: Races into trunk, displaying courage

indicators.note: into places the races inside the trunk

parts.note: a bole is a tree trunk
TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Cars race into a tree trunk, a display of bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race; 'into' puts it in BOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, nerve.

clue.text: Shocked at Turin Shroud, initially — one revealing body

indicators.note: shocked suggests letters thrown into disorder
initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at the Turin Shroud, a cloth said to show a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from Shroud; 'Shocked' rearranges it with AT TURIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is a nudist, someone who bares their body.

clue.text: Woman in wild is wild woman

indicators.note: in places the woman's name inside the word for wild

parts.note: wild and mad both mean frenzied
Ena is a woman's name, as in Ena Sharples of Coronation Street

explanation.surface: A woman who has gone wild is a wild woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena is a girl's name, best known from the British soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus, hence any frenzied woman.
